summary: Episode discusses the coronavirus-driven market crash in late February 2020, with OMXS30 down 11% for the week. Richard Bråse from DI analyzes the inverted yield curve, panic selling, and historical patterns. They discuss specific companies like Ratos as a cautionary tale of overvaluation and subsequent decline, and Swedish Match as a quality company. The conversation covers real estate sector being expensive, gaming stocks being undervalued, and upcoming macro indicators including employment data and purchasing manager indices. No explicit stock recommendations are made.
key_takeaways: OMXS30 was down 11% for the week during coronavirus panic in late February 2020
Inverted yield curve historically precedes market downturns but with a lag period of strong gains
Ratos serves as a case study of overvaluation leading to reckless acquisitions and eventual decline
Real estate sector considered expensive due to low interest rates driving valuations
Gaming stocks trading at very low valuations with investors ignoring cash flows
Market often blunders into accepting bad news about popular stocks for too long
Upcoming employment data and PMI indices will be important indicators of coronavirus economic impact
